newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-LEONARD DOING WHAT COMES NATURALLY BY FIGHTING AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-LEONARD DOING WHAT COMES NATURALLY BY FIGHTING AGAIN.

text.p: Forty-year-old five-time world champion Sugar Ray Leonard says he is only doing what comes naturally by ending six years of retirement to fight Hector "Macho" Camacho.

"I'm a fighter, this is what I do, this is what I enjoy doing, it's that simple," Leonard said at a news conference Thursday to officially announce his February 28 fight against Camacho in Atlantic City.
"Even at the age of 40 I know I'm capable of doing what I do best," said Leonard, a former welterweight, junior middleweight, middleweight, light heavyweight and super middleweight champion.
"I'm still healthy and I still feel that I can make a difference with those guys. I can still contend with these guys."

Leonard, 36-2-1, first quit in 1982 with a detached retina and then again two years later out of frustration with how he was fighting. He announced his last retirement after taking a terrible beating in losing to Terry Norris in February 1991 at Madison Square Garden.
But he said he had been toying for the last three years with the idea of fighting again.
"Athletes will always feel that they still have one last fight. I'm no different," Leonard said.
Leonard realised, though, he couldn't wait forever to make a comeback, so when Camacho proposed this fight earlier this year, the timing was just right.
"When I hit my 40th birthday I said, if I don't do it now, you never will do it," Leonard said.
Camacho, 63-3-1, said he was not surprised when Leonard decided to accept a fight against him.
"He does want to come back and be the darling boy," said the 34-year-old Camacho, a former lightweight, super featherweight and junior welterweight champion.

"He wants the action, he wants to come out and control the show like he used to," Camacho said of the charismatic Leonard. "He thinks he is going to come back and the public will say, wow, Ray is back. But there is too much competition out there now. Who needs Ray?
"It's my show now," said Camacho, who earlier this year outpointed another boxing legend, Roberto Duran, over 12 rounds.
Leonard is getting paid $5 million and Camacho's purse is $2 million.

Leonard, who said a substantial portion of his purse will go to the Sugar Ray Leonard Foundation to fight drugs and provide meals to needy children, left the door open about whether there would be more fights after this one.
"To say is this is a one-shot deal, I don't even talk about that. I do have ideas," Leonard said.
